paper.title_en: Toward Understanding the Emergence of the AdS/CFT Correspondence: A Constructive Perspective
paper.abstract_en: This dissertation presents a systematic study of the theoretical structure and origin of the AdS/CFT correspondence, addressing the fundamental question of why such a duality exists. We begin by establishing the necessary foundations, including conformal field theory, bulk-boundary correspondence in AdS spacetime, and supersymmetry. These concepts form the essential framework for understanding both sides of the duality. Next, from a higher-dimensional perspective, we explain the origins of the two sides: four-dimensional N=4 super Yang–Mills theory arises from the dimensional compactification of ten-dimensional super Yang–Mills theory, while Type II supergravity emerges as the low-energy effective theory of superstring theory and its dimensional compactification. Subsequently, using the D3 -brane system as the central object, we further reveal their unified string-theoretic origin of both sides. On the one hand, the open string degrees of freedom attached to the D3 -brane give rise to the worldvolume gauge theory; on the other hand, the closed string degrees of freedom describe supergravity background, and the corresponding supergravity solution in the near-horizon limit, yields the AdS5×S5 geometry, thereby connecting the two sides within a single framework. Finally, through parameter matching, symmetry correspondence, and operator mapping, the AdS/CFT naturally emerges, with the classical supergravity description is valid in the large N and strong coupling limit.
